data.cultural_impact: Ira is a name with rich cultural heritage in Hinduism. In Hindu mythology, the name Ira is revered as the symbol of wisdom and knowledge. Ira is derived from the Vedas and finds mention in various Hindu texts and scriptures. The name is often associated with Saraswati, the goddess of learning, music, and the arts. Therefore, the name is considered auspicious and carries a deep cultural significance for Hindu families, especially those with a focus on tradition and spirituality.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Ira represents the divine essence of wisdom and knowledge. It is believed that a girl named Ira is born with great intellectual potential, and her name is a constant reminder to strive for knowledge and wisdom throughout her life. Saraaswati, the deity associated with Ira, symbolizes purity, creativity, and knowledge. By bestowing this name on a child, parents are invoking the blessings of Saraswati, hoping that their child will grow up to be a wise and knowledgeable individual who uses her talents to make a positive impact on the world.

historical_references.reference: Ira was the name of a celestial nymph, or apsara, in Hindu mythology, commonly identified as the personification of the rainbow. She was the wife of the god Surya, the sun deity, and the mother of the twins Yama and Yami.
historical_references.time_period: Vedic and Post-Vedic periods (1500 BCE – 500 CE)

historical_references.reference: Ira was also the name of a queen of the Vangala people, who ruled the territory around modern-day Vijayawada in the Andhra region of India, during the Satavahana Empire (230 BCE – 220 CE). She is known for her military campaigns and her patronage of Buddhism.
